subsystems.name: Excavation plant
subsystems.role: moves very large volumes of dry, abrasive regolith at low gravity.

subsystems.name: Volatile extraction retort
subsystems.role: heats regolith in a sealed vessel to drive off implanted solar-wind gases.

subsystems.name: Gas separation and cryogenics
subsystems.role: separates helium from other evolved gases and then He-3 from He-4.

subsystems.name: Surface power and heat rejection
subsystems.role: the plant needs megawatts of steady power and must dump waste heat by radiation only.
parts: fission surface reactor or large solar array

subsystems.name: Lunar base and logistics
subsystems.role: habitation, landing pads and propellant for the whole operation.
parts: oxygen and water extraction from regolith

subsystems.name: Earth-return chain
subsystems.role: brings small masses of product back down safely.

subsystems.name: Consumer reactor
subsystems.role: the second half of the idea — a fusion machine that burns deuterium with He-3.

buildSteps.title: Assay the resource
buildSteps.detail: Return and analyse samples to map He-3 concentration, which runs at only a few tens of parts per billion by mass and is higher in titanium-rich mare soils.

buildSteps.title: Prove extraction in vacuum
buildSteps.detail: Heat regolith simulant in a vacuum chamber, measure how much helium evolves and at what temperature, and how much energy that costs per gram recovered.

buildSteps.title: Land a robotic pilot plant
buildSteps.detail: Place a small excavator and retort on the surface, powered by a fission reactor or a solar array, and process a few tonnes of real regolith.

buildSteps.title: Scale up mining and processing
buildSteps.detail: Because the grade is so low, one kilogram of He-3 needs on the order of 100,000 tonnes of regolith processed, so throughput — not chemistry — is the hard part.

buildSteps.title: Separate the isotopes
buildSteps.detail: Cool the evolved gas to a few kelvin so He-3 and He-4 can be separated cryogenically, then store the He-3 under pressure or as a liquid.

buildSteps.title: Return product to Earth
buildSteps.detail: Launch canisters on a lander's ascent stage — the mass is tiny, but the launch cost per trip is not.

buildSteps.title: Build something that burns it
buildSteps.detail: Develop a deuterium–He-3 reactor, which needs roughly ten times the plasma temperature of deuterium–tritium and has never been built.

buildSteps.title: Close the economics
buildSteps.detail: Only a working advanced-fusion fleet, or a large non-fusion market, would justify the mining rate.

prerequisites.why: it is the intended use, and no machine has ever ignited this fuel; the D–D side reactions also produce neutrons, so it is not fully aneutronic.

prerequisites.tech: Very high plasma temperatures and confinement
prerequisites.why: D–He-3 needs ion temperatures far above the ~10–15 keV that deuterium–tritium requires, roughly 100 keV.
reactor concepts for the lunar surface have been tested on the ground but not flown and operated.

prerequisites.tech: Large-scale lunar excavation and volatile extraction
prerequisites.why: oxygen-from-regolith and water-ice extraction have been demonstrated in the lab and in small field tests, not at mining rates.
robotic landers now reach the surface, but the cost per kilogram still makes bulk material handling prohibitive.
cryogenic distillation works industrially on Earth, but flight-qualified plant for lunar conditions does not exist.

pathway.milestone: Sample analysis and laboratory extraction experiments on regolith simulants
pathway.unlocks: a real number for grade, yield and energy cost per gram.

pathway.milestone: Lunar prospecting and a robotic extraction pilot, likely piggybacking on oxygen and water-ice mining that must heat regolith anyway
pathway.unlocks: He-3 as a by-product rather than the reason for the mission.

pathway.milestone: Surface fission power and mining at kilotonne scale
pathway.unlocks: enough throughput to think about kilograms per year.

pathway.milestone: A working deuterium–He-3 fusion machine, or a growing non-fusion market such as cryogenics for quantum computing
